A survey of $150$ randomly selected students at a particular university showed that only $24$ select at least one math course. Find a $95%$ confidence interval for the proportion of students from the entire university who select at least one math course. You may assume that the population size is significantly larger than the sample size.

*Hint: Given a random variable $Z∼N(0, 1)$, the table below shows the $z$-scores $z_{p}$ such that $P(Z > z_{p}) = p$ for some particular values of $p$.*

| $p$ | $0.100$ | $0.050$ | $0.025$ | $0.010$ | $0.005$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| $z_{p}$ | $1.282$ | $1.645$ | $1.960$ | $2.326$ | $2.576$ |

> A scientific calculator is required to answer this question.
